h1: 130 Hotel & Residence Bangkok — 4-Star Value on Ladprao 130 with MRT at Your Door
intro: Tucked into the residential calm of Soi Ladprao 130, 130 Hotel & Residence Bangkok has quietly built a loyal following among business travellers and Bangkok locals alike. Its 168 rooms run larger than the city average — Superior at 30 sqm, Deluxe at 40 sqm — with comfortable beds and genuinely warm service that consistently tops the review scores. MRT Yellow Line Ladprao 101 station is a five-minute walk away, linking the hotel to Ratchadaphisek interchange and onward to Sukhumvit, Silom or Suvarnabhumi Airport. From approx. ฿700/night.

body.html: Soi Ladprao 130 — also known as Ramkhamhaeng 81 — is the kind of Bangkok side street that doesn't make the tourist maps: low-rise shophouses, a 7-Eleven, a neighbourhood noodle shop, and a Lotus supermarket a short walk away. 130 Hotel & Residence opened here in 2016 and renovated in 2019 with a clear proposition: proper four-star comfort in a part of the city where most visitors never think to look. The result is 168 rooms that give you more space per baht than almost anything comparable in central Bangkok.

Every review category on Booking.com and Trip.com tells the same story, but the standout number is service: 8.8–8.9 out of 10 across both platforms. Guests describe staff who resolve check-in hiccups quickly, accommodate late check-out requests with good humour, and greet returning visitors by name. The on-site Indigo Restaurant serves a buffet breakfast (Thai, Chinese and Western selections) for just ฿120 per person — a figure that comes up in nearly every positive review mentioning value for money.
"Clean room, very soft bed, and incredibly friendly staff — always ready to help. Close to 7-Eleven, Lotus, and the MRT. Way better value than I expected."

The transport connection is the hotel's strongest practical card. MRT Yellow Line station Ladprao 101 is roughly a five-minute walk from the front door. From there you can ride to the Blue/Yellow interchange at Ratchadaphisek, then continue to Asok (Sukhumvit), Silom, or transfer toward Suvarnabhumi Airport — all without touching a taxi or Grab. The Mall Bangkapi — a full-scale lifestyle mall with a supermarket, cinema, restaurants and the HarborLand water park — sits about 2.5 km away, reachable in under 10 minutes by Grab.

The Bang Kapi neighbourhood has a character that central Bangkok shopping districts lack: a morning market, pavement noodle stalls, new-wave cafes opening along the soi, and Lotus Bangkapi within easy walking distance of the hotel entrance. For travellers visiting family or attending meetings in the Bangkapi–Ladprao corridor, this is four-star accommodation that the inner-city equivalents cannot match on price — or parking.

The honest caveats: parking is limited, so driving guests should notify the hotel in advance. Lower-floor rooms facing the main road can catch traffic noise at night — request a higher floor or an inner-facing room when you book. A handful of reviews mention WiFi needing a reconnect after extended use on certain floors. And one cluster of Trip.com reviews flagged a pest concern; the hotel responded publicly with a commitment to pest-control follow-up. Not dealbreakers, but worth knowing.

A score of 8.1 on Booking.com (585 reviews) and 8.8 on Trip.com (1,039 reviews) is a consistent double-platform endorsement that's hard to fake. 130 Hotel & Residence is not a lobby-photo hotel — it doesn't have a rooftop pool or a designer bar. What it delivers is clean, spacious rooms, a staff that actually cares, a walkable MRT connection, and prices that still feel like a bargain for a legitimate four-star. For anyone with business or family ties in the eastern Bangkok suburbs, this is an easy recommendation.

honestSummary: 130 Hotel & Residence Bangkok is the smart pick for travellers who need a comfortable four-star base in Bang Kapi without paying central Bangkok prices. Great service, generous room sizes and a walkable MRT connection are its three pillars — just don't expect a lifestyle hotel if Sukhumvit is your daily destination.
honestChecks: If you plan to visit Siam, Sukhumvit or the Old City every day — the Ladprao 130 address means 30–45 minutes each way on the MRT. For that itinerary, a hotel closer to BTS Sukhumvit will save you more time than this one saves you money.
If you're arriving by car and need guaranteed parking — spaces are limited; call ahead to confirm availability before you drive in.
If you need absolute quiet — request a higher floor or an inner soi-facing room when booking; street-level rooms on the Ladprao side can be noisy after dark.

tips.title: Use the MRT Yellow Line
tips.body: Walk 5 minutes to Ladprao 101 station. Change at Ratchadaphisek for the Blue Line — Asok/Sukhumvit in around 20 minutes, or continue to Suvarnabhumi Airport via Airport Rail Link interchange.

tips.title: Ask for a High Floor, Inner-Facing Room
tips.body: Rooms on floor 5 and above, facing away from the Ladprao main road, are significantly quieter. Mention this preference when booking or at check-in — staff are accommodating.

tips.title: Everything You Need Is Nearby
tips.body: 7-Eleven and Amazon Cafe are steps from the front door. Lotus Bangkapi (large supermarket) is a short walk. The Mall Bangkapi (full shopping mall) is 10 minutes by Grab.

tips.title: The ฿120 Breakfast Is Worth It
tips.body: Indigo Restaurant's buffet breakfast costs just ฿120 per person and covers Thai, Chinese and Western options. Families in particular find it more convenient and cost-effective than heading out.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — 130 Hotel & Residence Bangkok

faq.q: Where is 130 Hotel & Residence Bangkok located? Is it near an MRT station?
faq.a: The hotel is at 25 Soi Lat Phrao 130, Khlong Chan, Bang Kapi, Bangkok 10240. MRT Yellow Line station Ladprao 101 is approximately a five-minute walk away. From there you can connect to the Blue Line at Ratchadaphisek for onward travel to Sukhumvit, Silom or Suvarnabhumi Airport.

faq.q: How much does a room at 130 Hotel Bangkok cost?
faq.a: Room rates start from approximately ฿700–฿900/night for a Superior Room, and ฿900–฿1,200 for a Deluxe Room, depending on dates and booking platform. Prices vary seasonally, so comparing across Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com before booking is worthwhile.

faq.q: Who is 130 Hotel Bangkok best suited for?
faq.a: Business travellers with meetings in the Bangkapi–Ladprao corridor, families visiting relatives in east Bangkok, and value-conscious travellers who want genuine four-star comfort without paying central Bangkok rates. It's less ideal for tourists who plan to visit Siam or the Old City every day.

faq.q: Does 130 Hotel Bangkok have parking and a gym?
faq.a: Yes to both. Free on-site parking is available but limited — notify the hotel in advance if you're arriving by car. The fitness centre is free for all guests throughout their stay.

faq.q: How is the breakfast at 130 Hotel Bangkok?
faq.a: Indigo Restaurant serves a buffet breakfast for ฿120 per person, covering Thai, Chinese and Western options. Guest reviews consistently rate it as good value, particularly for families or anyone who prefers not to venture out first thing.

Best for business travellers and families in east Bangkok rather than those touring the city centre daily.
